negative_reviews.author: Vincent Yip
negative_reviews.text: I went there hoping to celebrate my wife's birthday. We were hoping that it will be proper Japanese Omakase. Unfortunately, the experience was far from perfect. The food was ok, i.e. acceptable, but nothing spectacular as described by other reviews. Service is ok, but again, nothing special. This is an average Japanese restaurant. Unfortunately, we won't go there again.

negative_reviews.author: EMG
negative_reviews.text: I want to preface my review of this restaurant by giving a mention to the two very welcoming staff members who were the reason my friend and I made the visit to Maki Nori. The staff were great, I can’t fault the service and the atmosphere inside was warm and provides a space that a real omakase restaurant does but I can’t help but feel there was a bit of false advertisement going on. The food was nothing special. My friend and I got the 15 piece ‘omakase’ but it came all on one plate? The quality of fish was so average and borderline not fresh, but it might have been different for the more expensive cuts of fish like the Chutoro tuna that I saw other people order. The fish that featured on the ‘omakase’ set was average at best - we were really surprised when it arrived. The lemon zest on the salmon nigiri added nothing and seemed like an attempt to fancify a simple item that needed no embellishment had the fish quality been at a certain standard. To provide a comparison, Eat Tokyo’s quality of fish is much better and sits at a better price range but I guess the atmosphere is something new…

negative_reviews.author: Nati Abay
negative_reviews.text: I went with my daughter, not only was wait time extremely long but the salmon avacado roll tasted unfresh and too fishy.
